\section[il bilancio]{il bilancio — the budget, the balance sheet; the assessment}

\label{lesson:IT-C394-bilancio}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for the punishment, then the Italian for the sanction.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: il bilancio}
\textbf{il bilancio} — \textquotedblleft{}the budget, the balance sheet; the assessment\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Se spendiamo così, il bilancio di casa non regge.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{If we spend like this, the household budget will not hold up.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Fare un bilancio} — to take stock. A company's yearly accounts are \emph{il bilancio}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{bilancio} is built on \emph{bilanciare} \textquotedblleft{}to balance\textquotedblright{}, from \emph{bilancia} \textquotedblleft{}scales\textquotedblright{}, inherited from Vulgar Latin \emph{bilancia}, from Latin \emph{bilanx} \textquotedblleft{}having two scale pans\textquotedblright{}, built from \emph{bi-} and \emph{lanx} \textquotedblleft{}a dish\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{il bilancio}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{il bilancio}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{il bilancio}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Italian for the punishment, then the Italian for the sanction, then say \emph{il bilancio} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does il bilancio mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The budget, the balance sheet; the assessment\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[il reddito]{il reddito — the income}

\label{lesson:IT-C394-reddito}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for the sanction, then the Italian for the budget.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: il reddito}
\textbf{il reddito} — \textquotedblleft{}the income\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Le tasse dipendono dal reddito.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Taxes depend on income.}
\end{quote}

Stress on the first syllable: \emph{rèddito}. \emph{La dichiarazione dei redditi} — the tax return.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{reddito} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{redditus} \textquotedblleft{}given back, returned\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short), past participle of \emph{reddere} \textquotedblleft{}to give back\textquotedblright{}, built on \emph{dare} \textquotedblleft{}to give\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{il reddito}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{il reddito}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{il reddito}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Italian for the sanction, then the Italian for the budget, then say \emph{il reddito} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does il reddito mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The income\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[la bolletta]{la bolletta — the utility bill}

\label{lesson:IT-C394-bolletta}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for the budget, then the Italian for the income.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la bolletta}
\textbf{la bolletta} — \textquotedblleft{}the utility bill\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Se non paghi la bolletta, ti tagliano la luce.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{If you do not pay the bill, they cut off your electricity.}
\end{quote}

For electricity, gas, water or phone; at a restaurant it is \emph{il conto}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{bolletta} is a little \emph{bolla} \textquotedblleft{}seal, stamped paper\textquotedblright{}, inherited from Latin \emph{bulla} \textquotedblleft{}a bubble, a knob, a seal\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB): first a stamped receipt.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{la bolletta}, once more

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Italian for the budget, then the Italian for the income, then say \emph{la bolletta} again
\end{itemize}

\section[il canone]{il canone — the regular fee, the rent; the canon}

\label{lesson:IT-C394-canone}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for the income, then the Italian for the utility bill.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: il canone}
\textbf{il canone} — \textquotedblleft{}the regular fee, the rent; the canon\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Il canone d'affitto aumenta ogni anno.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The rent goes up every year.}
\end{quote}

Stress on the first syllable: \emph{cànone}. \emph{Il canone} of the state TV is a yearly licence fee.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{canone} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{canōn}, from Greek \emph{kan\'{\={o}}n} \textquotedblleft{}a measuring rod, a standard\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB): a fixed rule, then a fixed payment.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[il mutuo]{il mutuo — the mortgage, the (bank) loan}

\label{lesson:IT-C394-mutuo}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for the utility bill, then the Italian for the regular fee.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: il mutuo}
\textbf{il mutuo} — \textquotedblleft{}the mortgage, the (bank) loan\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Se la banca ci dà il mutuo, compriamo la casa.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{If the bank gives us the mortgage, we will buy the house.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Pagare il mutuo} — to pay the mortgage. As an adjective it means mutual.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{mutuo} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{mūtuum} \textquotedblleft{}a loan\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short), from \emph{mūtuus} \textquotedblleft{}borrowed, lent; in return, mutual\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{il mutuo}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{il mutuo}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{il mutuo}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Italian for the utility bill, then the Italian for the regular fee, then say \emph{il mutuo} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[(dialogue)]{Ripasso dei capitoli 387–394}

\label{lesson:IT-R394-ripasso-387-394}



\begin{quote}
Say the Italian for the requirement and suitable.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item the requirement, suitable, the admission, to exclude, the condition
  \item to expire, valid, to renew, the renewal, the card
  \item the bureaucracy, the paperwork, the procedure, the request, the certificate
  \item legal, illegal, permissible, unlawful, unauthorised
  \item to accuse, the accusation, the thief, the criminal complaint, the corruption
  \item the defendant, the defence, the verdict, the conviction, the penalty
  \item the prison, the prisoner, to punish, the punishment, the sanction
  \item the budget, the income, the utility bill, the regular fee, the mortgage
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
The requirement? (\textbf{il requisito}.) Suitable? (\textbf{idoneo}.) The admission? (\textbf{l'ammissione}.) To exclude? (\textbf{escludere}.) The condition? (\textbf{la condizione}.) To expire? (\textbf{scadere}.) Valid? (\textbf{valido}.) To renew? (\textbf{rinnovare}.) The renewal? (\textbf{il rinnovo}.) The card? (\textbf{la tessera}.) The bureaucracy? (\textbf{la burocrazia}.) The paperwork? (\textbf{la pratica}.) The procedure? (\textbf{la procedura}.) The request? (\textbf{la richiesta}.) The certificate? (\textbf{il certificato}.) Legal? (\textbf{legale}.) Illegal? (\textbf{illegale}.) Permissible? (\textbf{lecito}.) Unlawful? (\textbf{illecito}.) Unauthorised? (\textbf{abusivo}.) To accuse? (\textbf{accusare}.) The accusation? (\textbf{l'accusa}.) The thief? (\textbf{il ladro}.) The criminal complaint? (\textbf{la querela}.) The corruption? (\textbf{la corruzione}.) The defendant? (\textbf{l'imputato}.) The defence? (\textbf{la difesa}.) The verdict? (\textbf{la sentenza}.) The conviction? (\textbf{la condanna}.) The penalty? (\textbf{la pena}.) The prison? (\textbf{il carcere}.) The prisoner? (\textbf{il detenuto}.) To punish? (\textbf{punire}.) The punishment? (\textbf{la punizione}.) The sanction? (\textbf{la sanzione}.) The budget? (\textbf{il bilancio}.) The income? (\textbf{il reddito}.) The utility bill? (\textbf{la bolletta}.) The regular fee? (\textbf{il canone}.) The mortgage? (\textbf{il mutuo}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
